To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rat brain Na+ (voltage-sensitive) channel mRNAs are expressed in astrocytes in both in vivo and in cultured astrocytes.
rat brain subtype I, II and III Na+ mRNA are detected in astrocytes in culture and in optic nerve.
astrocytes express voltage-sensitive Na(+) channel messages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of Na+ channel mNAs in astrocytic and neuronal cells in the central and peripheral nervous systems.
the molecular characterization of Na+ channel subunit expression in rat CNS astrocytes.
the expression of Na+ channel mNAs in rat astrocyte in vivo and in culture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of voltage-sensitive Na+ currents in astrocytes is not due to the presence of neuronal-type Na+ channels.
the three types of Na+ channel mRNNAs are present in rat brain and skeletal muscle, and in rat astrocyte cultures.
the Na+ channels expressed by CNS astrocytes are not identical with the Na+ channels of skeletal muscle, liver, or brain neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
astrocytes express Na+ channel mRNAS which are identical to those in neurons.
astrocytes express Na+ channel subunits which are similar to those expressed by neurons.
rat brain voltage-sensitive sodium channel mRNAs can be detected in astrocytes, and that these astrocytes may express all three types of sodium channel mRNas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
astrocytes can express Na+ channels.
astrocytes are not just a passive component of the nervous system, but are also an important component of the nervous tissue.
the Na+ channel expression in astrocytes is more complicated than previously thought.
